Makkan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Allah did not mention in this surah except the story of Nuh alone, because of the length of his stay among his people and the repetition of his call to monotheism and his prohibition of shirk (association of partners with Allah).

{2–4} Nuh, peace be upon him, complied with this and hastened to the command of Allah, and said: {O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner}; i.e., one whose warning is evident and manifest. That is for his clarifying what he warned about and what he warned against, and by what means salvation is attained. He explained this with a complete and sufficient explanation: he informed them and commanded them with the foundation of that, saying: {that you worship Allah and fear Him}. This means singling Him out for worship, affirming His unity, and keeping far from shirk and its paths and means. For when they fear Allah, He forgives their sins; and when He forgives their sins, they attain salvation from punishment and success with reward. {And He will postpone you to a specified term}; i.e., He will let you enjoy this abode and will ward off destruction from you until a specified term, i.e., a lifespan in this world determined by the decree and destiny of Allah up to a limited time. The enjoyment is not forever, for death is inevitable. Therefore He said: {Indeed, the term of Allah, when it comes, is not postponed, if you only knew}, just as you disbelieved in Allah and defied the truth.

{5–7} They did not respond to his call nor submitted to his command. So he complained to his Lord, saying: {My Lord, indeed I have invited my people night and day. But my invitation has increased them only in flight}; i.e., aversion from the truth and turning away. So there was no benefit in that, for the benefit of calling is that all or some of the intended goal be achieved. {And indeed, whenever I invited them that You might forgive them}; i.e., in order that they might respond; for if they respond, You will forgive them. This was purely for their benefit, but they refused, except to persist in their falsehood and flee from the truth. {They put their fingers in their ears} out of fear of hearing what their prophet Nuh said to them, {and covered themselves with their garments}; i.e., they wrapped themselves in them as a covering that veiled them, out of distance from the truth and hatred of it. {And persisted} in their disbelief and evil, {and were arrogant} toward the truth {with great arrogance}. So their evil increased and their good diminished.

{8–9} {Then indeed I invited them openly}; i.e., within the hearing of all of them. {Then I announced to them and I spoke to them secretly in private}. All of this was out of eagerness and sincere counsel, and bringing them by every means that might be thought to achieve the goal.

{10–12} {So I said: Seek forgiveness from your Lord}; i.e., abandon the sins you are upon and seek Allah's forgiveness for them; {indeed He is Ever-Forgiving}: abundantly forgiving to whoever repents and seeks forgiveness. He encouraged them with the forgiveness of sins and what follows from it of reward and the removal of punishment. He also encouraged them with the immediate good of this world, saying: {He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain}; i.e., continuous rain that quenches the valleys and lowlands and gives life to the lands and the servants. {And provide you with wealth and children}; i.e., increase your wealth, by which you attain what you seek of this world, and your children. {And make for you gardens and make for you rivers}. This is among the most eloquent of the pleasures and aims of this world.

{13–14} {What is the matter with you that you do not attribute to Allah any dignity?}; i.e., you do not fear Allah's greatness, and Allah has no regard in your eyes. {While He has created you in stages}; i.e., creating you stage after stage: in the mother's womb, then in nursing, then in childhood, then discernment, then youth, and then to the last stage that creation reaches. Therefore He who alone creates and disposes with wondrous wisdom is necessarily to be singled out for worship and affirmation of unity. In mentioning the beginning of their creation is a reminder to them about the Return (ma'ad), and that He who brought them into existence from nothing is capable of restoring them after their death.

{15–16} He also argued from the creation of the heavens, which are greater than the creation of humans, saying: {Do you not see how Allah created seven heavens in layers}; i.e., each heaven above the other. {And made the moon therein a light}: for the people of the earth, {and made the sun a lamp}. In this is an indication of the greatness of the creation of these things and the abundance of benefits in the sun and moon, which point to Allah's mercy and the vastness of His kindness. The Mighty, the Merciful, deserves to be magnified, loved, feared, and hoped in.

{17–18} {And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth as growth}: when He created your father Adam while you were in his loins. {Then He will return you into it}: at death, {and bring you forth}: for resurrection and gathering. He is the One who owns life, death, and resurrection.

{19–20} {And Allah has made for you the earth a spread-out expanse}; i.e., spread out and prepared for benefit from it, {that you may take therein roads of passage}. Had He not spread it out, that would not have been possible; indeed, they could not have tilled it, planted it, sown it, built upon it, or dwelt upon its surface.

{21–24} {Nuh said}, complaining to his Lord: indeed this speech, admonition, and reminder had no effect upon them and was of no benefit: {Indeed, they have disobeyed me} in what I commanded them, {and followed one whose wealth and children increase him only in loss}; i.e., they disobeyed the sincere messenger who guides to good, and followed the chiefs and nobles whose wealth and children increased them only in loss, i.e., ruin and the squandering of profits. How then of one who submits to them and obeys them? {And they have plotted a great plot}; i.e., a great and grave plot in opposing the truth. They said to them, calling to shirk and adorning it for them: {Do not leave your gods}. They urged them to zealous adherence to what they were upon of shirk, and not to abandon what their forefathers had been upon. Then they specified their gods, saying: {Neither Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth, nor Ya'uq, nor Nasr}. These were names of righteous men; when they died, Satan adorned for their people the making of their images, so that they would be enlivened, by their claim, to obedience upon seeing them. Then time lengthened and others came, and Satan said to them: Your forefathers worshipped them, sought intercession through them, and by them rain was sent down. So they worshipped them. For this reason their leaders enjoined on their followers that they not abandon the worship of these idols. {And they have already misled many}; i.e., the great ones and leaders, by their call, misled many of the creatures. {And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error}; i.e., had their error been, at my calling them to the truth, a benefit, it would have been good; but they increase, through the call of their leaders, only in error. That is, there remained no place for their success and righteousness.

{25} For this reason Allah mentioned their punishment and worldly and otherworldly retribution, saying: {Because of their sins they were drowned}: in the sea that encompassed them, {and then were admitted to Fire}: so their bodies perished in the drowning and their spirits were taken to the Fire and burning. All this was because of their sins, about which their prophet [Nuh] came to warn them and inform them of their evil and consequence. They rejected what he said until retribution befell them. {And they found for themselves, other than Allah, no helpers}: who could support them when the grievous matter descended upon them, and no one can oppose the decree and destiny.

{26–27} {And Nuh said: My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers, any dweller}: one who moves about on the face of the earth. He mentioned the reason for this, saying: {Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except wicked disbelievers}; i.e., their survival is pure corruption for them and for others. Nuh said this because, despite his long association with them and his constant dealing with their conduct, he knew from that the outcome of their deeds. Therefore Allah answered his supplication and drowned them all, and saved Nuh and those believers with him.

{28} {My Lord, forgive me, my parents, and whoever enters my house as a believer}: he specified those mentioned to affirm their right and to prioritize their kindness. Then he generalized the supplication, saying: {And the believing men and believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in ruin}; i.e., loss, destruction, and perdition.

End of the tafsir of Surah Nuh. And praise be to Allah.
